bib.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks

question: Can a generator redesigned around style transfer (AdaIN, learned constant input, per-layer noise) give better image quality and a more controllable, less entangled latent space than the traditional GAN generator?
hypothesis: An intermediate latent space W, free from having to follow the training-data density, can be less entangled than the input space Z, and the synthesis network favours a disentangled representation.
contributions: A style-based generator: mapping network Z to W, AdaIN at every convolution, learned constant input, per-layer noise inputs
Mixing regularization that decorrelates neighbouring styles and enables scale-specific control
Two automated, encoder-free metrics: perceptual path length and linear separability
The FFHQ dataset of 70,000 faces at 1024x1024

method.summary: The generator of Progressive GAN is rebuilt: an 8-layer MLP maps z to w, learned affine transforms turn w into per-layer AdaIN scale and bias, synthesis starts from a learned 4x4x512 constant, and Gaussian noise is added after each convolution. Discriminator and loss are unchanged. Quality is measured by FID, latent-space quality by perceptual path length and linear separability.
method.task: unconditional image synthesis with GANs (faces, bedrooms, cars, cats)

datasets.name: FFHQ
datasets.split: FID uses 50,000 images drawn randomly from the training set
datasets.source: crawled from Flickr, permissive licences only, aligned and cropped, filtered with Mechanical Turk; public
datasets.preprocessing: automatic alignment [31] and cropping; mirror augmentation enabled

datasets.name: CelebA-HQ
datasets.source: Karras et al. [30]; also supplies 40 attribute labels for classifiers

datasets.name: LSUN Bedroom, Cars, Cats
datasets.preprocessing: mirror augmentation disabled; Bedroom and Cats at 256x256, Cars at 512x384

models.name: Style-based generator (config F)
models.architecture: 8-layer MLP mapping network (512-d z and w); 18-layer synthesis network, two layers per resolution 4x4 to 1024x1024; AdaIN after each convolution; learned 4x4x512 constant input; per-layer noise; 1x1 conv to RGB

models.name: Traditional generator (config B / Progressive GAN)
models.architecture: latent fed through input layer only

models.name: Attribute classifiers (40, one per CelebA attribute)
models.architecture: discriminator architecture with minibatch standard deviation disabled

training.objective: CelebA-HQ: WGAN-GP; FFHQ: WGAN-GP for config A, non-saturating loss with R1 regularization (gamma = 10) for configs B-F
training.optimizer: Adam, hyperparameters inherited from Progressive GAN [30]; exponential moving average of generator
training.lr: same as Progressive GAN for FFHQ; 0.002 instead of 0.003 for 512^2 and 1024^2 on CelebA-HQ; mapping network lr = 0.01 x lr
training.lr_schedule: inferred: resolution-dependent as in Progressive GAN; not detailed here
training.batch_size: resolution-dependent minibatch sizes inherited from [30]; values not given
training.regularisation: R1 (gamma 10); mixing regularization (0/50/90/100% of training examples); equalized learning rate; no batch norm, spectral norm, attention or pixelwise feature vector normalization
training.hardware: NVIDIA DGX-1 with 8 Tesla V100 GPUs
training.compute: approximately one week on a DGX-1

other.images seen LSUN: 70M for Bedroom and Cats, 46M for Cars
other.progressive growing: starts from 8x8 images instead of 4x4; full 1024 resolution reached at 8.4M images (Fig 9)
other.bilinear up/down: separable 2nd order binomial filter after each upsampling and before each downsampling [64]
other.init: weights N(0,1); constant input initialised to one; biases and noise scaling zero, except biases for y_s set to one
other.mapping depth: deeper mapping made training unstable at high lr, hence 0.01x lr

inference.samples: FID on 50,000 images, lowest distance during training reported; PPL 100,000 samples; separability 200,000 generated images, least confident half dropped

parameters.truncation psi: w' = w_bar + psi(w - w_bar); psi=0.7 applied for resolutions 4^2-32^2 in figures only
parameters.mixing: random crossover point between w1 and w2

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet inception distance [25] on 50,000 generated images vs training set; lowest value over training

metrics.name: Perceptual path length (full / end)
metrics.definition: expected VGG16-based perceptual distance [65] between images at t and t+eps along slerp (Z) or lerp (W) interpolation, divided by eps^2; faces cropped; 'end' restricts t to {0,1}

metrics.name: Separability
metrics.definition: exp(sum_i H(Y_i|X_i)) over 40 attributes, X = linear SVM side, Y = classifier label

eval.protocol: single reported run per config; no seeds or significance tests stated

availability.weights: pre-trained networks released; classifier networks to be released

results.claim: Each stage from baseline Progressive GAN to full style-based generator lowers FFHQ FID, 8.04 to 4.40.
results.setup: FFHQ 1024^2, config F vs config A
results.table: Table 1, row F + Mixing regularization, column FFHQ; row A column FFHQ 8.04

results.claim: On CelebA-HQ FID falls from 7.79 (A) to 5.17 (F), best 5.06 at E.
Style-based generator (E) improves FID over the tuned traditional generator (B) by almost 20%.
Mixing regularization greatly improves FID when several latents are mixed at test time (4 latents: 17.41 without vs 9.03 at 90%).
results.note: Single-latent FID is 4.40 at 90% and 4.42 at 0%; 100% mixing hurts it (4.83).

results.claim: Full-path perceptual path length in W is much shorter with noise inputs (200.5) than the traditional generator in Z (412.0).
results.setup: FFHQ, config E in W vs B in Z
results.table: Table 3, row E + Add noise inputs, column full

results.claim: Linear separability is far better in W (3.61) than in Z of the traditional generator (10.78).
results.setup: FFHQ, config D in W vs B in Z
results.table: Table 3, row D Style-based generator W, column Separability

results.claim: Adding an 8-layer mapping network to a traditional generator wrecks separability in Z (170.29) but gives 6.52 in W.
results.table: Table 4, row Traditional 8 Z, column Separability
results.note: Path length in Z worsens from 412.0 to 896.2; FID 4.87.

results.claim: Deeper mapping network improves style-based FID: 4.60 (1 layer), 4.43 (2), 4.40 (8); 5.06 with none.
results.table: Table 4, row F Style-based 8 W, column FID

results.claim: Style-based generator has 26.2M parameters versus 23.1M for the traditional one.
FID on other LSUN sets with config F: Bedroom 2.65, Cars 3.27, Cats 8.53.
FID keeps decreasing under R1 while path length slowly rises, so FID gains come with a more entangled representation.

limits: Authors note the path-length metric measured over the full path is biased toward Z, since W may have regions off the input manifold.
Mixing regularization appears to distort W somewhat (path length rises from 200.5 to 234.0).
FID gains in training come with longer path lengths; whether this is unavoidable is left open.
LSUN Bedroom limited by compression artifacts in training data; Cats remains hard.
No seeds, variance, or significance reported; batch sizes and learning rates referenced to Progressive GAN rather than stated.
Truncation trick used only for figures; FIDs computed without it.
Dated: GAN-era unconditional synthesis; later diffusion models superseded it for text-to-image.

terms.definition: AdaIN(x_i, y) = y_s,i (x_i - mu(x_i))/sigma(x_i) + y_b,i; each feature map normalized separately then scaled and biased by the style
generating a fraction of training images from two latent codes, switching w1 to w2 at a random crossover point
w' = w_bar + psi(w - w_bar) with psi < 1, where w_bar is the mean of f(z)
average perceptual distance between images at nearby points along latent interpolation, scaled by 1/eps^2
exp(sum H(Y|X)) of how well a linear SVM in latent space predicts classifier labels
